subject: gate-harness-naming.v4
role: The D-086 successor owed by D-144 Decision 3 — the act that names the riding DR-133 NT classes at the DR-G20 and DR-G21 obligations.
verdictRule: ACCEPT only at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX. Measured: 0 blockers, 1 SHOULD-FIX, 1 advisory.
headline: The naming itself is exactly right and exactly bounded — I could not break it on any of the seven named attacks. What blocks is one stale pin: the artifact cites COORD at the digest it had one commit before the HEAD this review is conducted against.

environmentCustody.d144Adopted: verified in live COORD: one ## D-144 heading, ADOPTED at turn 2 with both reviewers at CONSENT, pinning my turn-2 verdict at 0f9d56d2, which matches my file

diffAudit.method: v4 was compared to v3 key by key and gate by gate, because a 22-gate naming artifact is exactly where a scoped successor could quietly change something else.

That is the DR-102 CC-1..CC-11 construction D-144 Decision 3 named as the model, applied without embellishment.

attacksRun.detail: Neither appears in either executes field. Both gates' doesNotClaim say 'Does not execute DR-133 NT-3 or NT-5' in terms, dr133Join lists them under stillLeftoverDesign, whatThisDoesNotDo says 'Does not name NT-3 or NT-5 at any gate', and remainingUnmetNamed records that a later leftover-design act remains for them. Four independent statements, all consistent.

attacksRun.detail: The DR-G10 entry is byte-identical to v3. No NT id appears in it.

attacksRun.detail: 22 gate ids in both versions, identical set; sliceScope.requiredNow is element-wise identical at 18 members; commissionNote states requiredNow remains 18 and the 16/18 arithmetic is unchanged; condition4EffectIfLaterRecorded is unchanged from v3.

attacksRun.detail: 'Does not close DR-133 leftover-design' and 'Does not make D-056 gates 2 or 3 hold by itself (naming is this act; leftover-design remains for NT-3/NT-5)' are both in whatThisDoesNotDo. The parenthetical is the honest formulation: this act supplies the naming half and says so without claiming the rest.
Every SATISFIED occurrence is a refusal, Class A does not occur at all, and both implementation/ occurrences are refusals.

attacksRun.detail: Twenty of twenty-two gate entries are byte-identical to v3; the two that changed are the two D-144 named, and each changed only in executes and doesNotClaim.

attacksRun.detail: gate-harness-naming.v3, provider-only-nt-gate-join.v6, provider-only-output-contract.v3 and file 08 all reproduce. COORD does not. Routed to CLAUDE-GHN-V4-SF1.

The narrowed recordedInputs leaves the inherited 22-gate table unevidenced

shouldFix.title: recordedInputs pins COORD at the digest it had one commit before the HEAD this artifact is reviewed against
shouldFix.finding: recordedInputs cites docs/coop/COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md at e75608e07cf4981e47e3b5e735a3a1b45f408f24f04fddb2d12448470fc3f311. Live COORD is e838775b3c47f4347b7bf5935711bbfa87e94fd5423317100d58cb78c6276341. I traced the movement: e75608e0 is COORD at 13b07f4, the D-144 adoption commit, and e838775b is COORD at 1ac85c7, the D-144 hygiene commit that removed a duplicate adopted heading. The dispatch and the review prompt both name 1ac85c7 as HEAD, so the artifact is being reviewed against a tree where its own COORD pin does not resolve. The other four file pins — v3, the v6 join, the v3 contract and file 08 — all reproduce exactly, and the D-144 commit pin 13b07f4 is correct, so this is the only one.
shouldFix.whyNotBlocker: The movement is provably scope-free. Removing a duplicate D-144 heading cannot touch any property a COORD pin supports here — the required-gate set, the SARIF-drop consequence, the D-006 runner class, or the D-086 commission. Nothing the artifact asserts becomes wrong.
shouldFix.whyChargedAtAll: The artifact will be frozen and recorded by a later D-000 entry that pins it and re-measures its inputs, at which point a COORD digest inside it that disagrees with the recording entry's own COORD pin is a visible inconsistency in the record. The artifact's remeasurementClause tells a reader what to do when a pin moves; it does not make a moved pin correct.
shouldFix.repair: Either re-measure COORD to e838775b, or add the clause the coordinator entries use for exactly this case: that COORD movement which is duplicate-heading hygiene or append-only growth, with file 08 and the cited artifacts unmoved, is PASS-NO-SCOPE-EFFECT and does not require a new version. The second option is the more durable, since COORD moves whenever anything is adopted.
evidence: measured: git show 13b07f4:COORD hashes to e75608e0; git show 1ac85c7:COORD hashes to e838775b; live COORD is e838775b
dispatch and review prompt: 'HEAD is 1ac85c7 (D-144 hygiene)'

advisories.title: propertyPins was dropped while the clause that depends on it was kept verbatim
advisories.finding: v3's recordedInputs carried a propertyPins entry naming what the pins were good for: 'D-001 condition 4 harness-half; D-002 required-gate set and G08/G09/G06/G11/G13 riders; D-002 SARIF-drop consequence; D-077 / DR-006 v2 SARIF_for_analyze DROPS; D-006 runner class, thresholds, machine-pin obligation, Intel procurability; file 08 22-gate table'. v4's recordedInputs has no such entry, but remeasurementClause is carried across byte-for-byte: 'If a cited file moves, re-measure. Pins support only the named properties.' No properties are now named, so the clause's second sentence has nothing to point at.
advisories.whyNotShouldFix: It cannot cause an over-claim. Read literally, pins that name no properties support nothing, which errs safe. And the artifact's substantive assertions rest on the predecessor pin and the two DR-133 artifacts, all of which reproduce.
advisories.repair: Restore a propertyPins entry scoped to what v4 actually relies on — the v3 commission and 22-gate table, the v6 riding assignment, and the v3 contract's NT classes — or drop the second sentence of remeasurementClause.

independence.otherReviewerHandling: No Codex file for this subject existed at review time; none was sought or opened.
independence.priorParticipation: I reviewed all six versions of the DR-133 gate join and both D-144 turns, and this artifact performs the act D-144 Decision 3 created at my prompting. That is the strongest reason to check it hardest rather than to wave through the act I asked for. The naming was therefore checked gate by gate against v3's bytes and against v6's riding map, not against my expectation of what it should say.

coordinatorSummary: REJECT at 0 blockers and 1 SHOULD-FIX, with one advisory. Twelve attacks run, two landed, neither touching the naming itself. Custody is clean: aa2bec2e at 0444 unmoved, dispatch and prompt agreeing, HEAD never left 1ac85c7, file 08 and the predecessor at their digests, and D-144 verified as ADOPTED in live COORD with my turn-2 verdict pinned at a digest that matches my file. The act is done correctly and I could not break it. Twenty of the twenty-two gate entries are byte-identical to v3; the two that changed are the two D-144 named, and each changed only in executes and doesNotClaim. DR-G21 now carries 'DR-133 NT-1, NT-2, NT-6 execute here (provider-only-output-contract.v3 / provider-only-nt-gate-join.v6)' in the same form as the CC-1..CC-11 sentence beside it, and DR-G20 carries the NT-4 and NT-7 equivalent — which is exactly the model D-144 Decision 3 specified. NT-3 and NT-5 are excluded four separate ways: both gates' doesNotClaim, dr133Join.stillLeftoverDesign, a new whatThisDoesNotDo refusal, and a new remainingUnmetNamed entry recording that a later leftover-design act remains. No gate row is added, requiredNow is element-wise identical at 18, the 16/18 arithmetic and condition4EffectIfLaterRecorded are untouched, no NT is assigned to G10, and whatThisDoesNotDo gained five refusals and lost none — including the honest 'Does not make D-056 gates 2 or 3 hold by itself'. What blocks is a single stale pin. recordedInputs cites COORD at e75608e0, which is COORD at 13b07f4, the D-144 adoption; the hygiene commit 1ac85c7 that both the dispatch and the prompt name as HEAD moved it to e838775b. The other four file pins and the D-144 commit pin all reproduce. The movement is provably scope-free — a duplicate-heading deletion cannot touch the required-gate set, the SARIF-drop consequence, the D-006 runner class or the D-086 commission — but the artifact will be frozen and recorded by an entry that re-measures, and a COORD digest inside it that disagrees with that entry's own pin is a visible inconsistency. Either re-measure, or add the PASS-NO-SCOPE-EFFECT clause the coordinator entries use, which is the more durable fix since COORD moves on every adoption. The advisory is that propertyPins was dropped while remeasurementClause still says pins support only the named properties, leaving that sentence with nothing to point at; it errs safe, so it does not block. Three items I considered and declined are recorded so the choices are auditable.
